g.data-info: A tough membrane of connective tissue covering the bone surface, containing cells that build new bone.
Dense, hard bone forming the outer shell, especially thick around the shaft, giving strength.
Soft tissue filling the spaces of spongy bone that makes red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.
A lightweight lattice of bony struts (trabeculae) in the ends of the bone, whose spaces hold red marrow.
The hollow centre of the shaft, filled with fatty yellow marrow that stores energy.
The remains of the growth plate where the bone grew in length; it becomes bone once growth stops.
Smooth, slippery hyaline cartilage covering the joint surfaces to reduce friction and absorb shock.
An artery that passes through a small hole in the shaft to supply the marrow and bone with blood.
The enlarged upper end of the femur, made mostly of spongy bone, that forms part of the hip joint.
The long, hollow shaft of the bone, made of a thick tube of compact bone around the medullary cavity.
The enlarged lower end of the femur that forms part of the knee joint.
